title: Debug a claim deductible settlement
tagline: Reproduce a support ticket, find why net payable goes negative, and fix the settlement rule.
intro: This round is a bug fix. ClaimSettlement.netPayable is producing impossible payouts on the finance report. I will give you the support ticket, the broken code, and the failing tests. Diagnose the root cause before you change anything.
reproductionNote: Support ticket FIN-4412: "Claim approved 500.00 with a 750.00 deductible settled as -250.00. A second claim approved 600.00 with deductible -100.00 settled as 700.00. Finance rejects both. A claim with no deductible pays correctly." Steps: run ClaimSettlement.netPayable with those pairs and compare with the settlement rules.

diagnosis.prompt: Explain the root cause in your own words: what assumption in netPayable is wrong, and what rule should replace it?
diagnosis.strongAnswer: The method subtracts any deductible, even when it exceeds the approved amount or is negative, so the result can go below zero or above the approved amount. Net payable must clamp to zero and treat a negative deductible as zero.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What exactly is net payable when the deductible is larger than the approved amount?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Approved minus deductible, but never below zero. If the deductible meets or exceeds the approved amount, net payable is zero.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask for the boundary rule instead of assuming plain subtraction.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How should a negative deductible or negative approved amount be treated?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: A negative approved amount settles to zero. A negative deductible is treated as zero, so the full approved amount is payable.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask about invalid money values, especially negative deductibles.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What follow-up change is coming?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Expect a batch method that settles many claims from two maps of approved amounts and deductibles, reusing the corrected single-claim rule.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask how the fixed rule will be reused by the follow-up.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Do you want a regression test for the ticket?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: The hidden suite includes a regression test that pins the deductible-exceeds-approved case. Reproduce it first so you can prove the fix.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask whether the ticket becomes a permanent regression test.

clarifyingFallback: Assume net payable is approved minus deductible, floored at zero, with non-positive approved amounts settling to zero and non-positive deductibles treated as zero. Reproduce the ticket before fixing.
problemStatement:
### Context

ClaimSettlement.netPayable is used by the finance report. A support ticket shows payouts that are negative or larger than the approved amount.

### Your task

Read the broken code, reproduce the failure, identify the root cause, and fix it without changing the method signature.

### Rules

- A null or non-positive approved amount settles to zero.
- A null or non-positive deductible is treated as zero.
- Net payable is approved minus deductible, but never below zero.
- Use BigDecimal arithmetic and do not round.

### Reproduction

The ticket and the failing test names are in the reproduction note above the editor. Start by explaining the failure, then fix it.

hiddenTests.name: normal deduction reduces the payout
matching deductible settles at zero
deductible above approved clamps to zero
null deductible pays the full approved amount
negative deductible and approved amounts are safe

changeRequest.prompt: Settle a batch of claims from approved and deductible maps.
changeRequest.statement:
### Change request

Finance now sends a batch of claims.

Add:

Map<String, BigDecimal> settleAll(Map<String, BigDecimal> approvedByClaim, Map<String, BigDecimal> deductibleByClaim)

Requirements:

- Return a TreeMap keyed by claim id, sorted ascending.
- Every approved claim id appears in the result, even when its approved amount is null or non-positive.
- A missing deductible for a claim is treated as zero.
- A null approved map returns an empty map.
- Reuse the corrected netPayable logic; do not duplicate the clamp rule.

hiddenTests.name: batch settlement returns clamped values in id order
batch settlement handles null maps and missing deductibles
batch settlement includes non-positive approvals

probes.text: Reproduce the ticket first. What is the smallest input that shows the defect?
State the root cause in your own words, then name the test that proves your fix.
Which existing behaviour could your clamp break, and which test guards it?

fallbackProbe: If you only fixed the subtraction, which second case in the ticket would still be wrong?

phasePrompts.brief: Read the ticket and the code, then ask me the questions you would ask a real interviewer. Reproduce the failure before editing.
phasePrompts.implement: The diagnosis timer is running. Narrate your hypotheses, isolate the defect, and say when you want to run the tests.
phasePrompts.test: Run the tests. Confirm the regression fails for the reason you predicted, then fix it.
phasePrompts.change: Here is the change request. Reuse the corrected rule rather than copying it.
phasePrompts.debrief: Time is up. Let us review the diagnosis, the fix, the regression test, and the rubric.

hints: Run the failing test first. Compare the actual value with the finance rule instead of reading the code top to bottom.
The defect is not the subtraction itself; it is the missing clamp and the treatment of a negative deductible.
Fix the single-claim rule, then call it from settleAll so the batch cannot drift from the base behaviour.

rubric.criterion: The defect is fixed and the hidden suite passes
rubric.strongAnswer: Net payable clamps at zero, treats a negative deductible as zero, and handles null inputs safely.

rubric.criterion: Batch settlement passes the hidden suite
rubric.strongAnswer: The batch method is sorted, null-safe, includes every approved id, and reuses the corrected rule.
Names the missing clamp and the negative-deductible assumption, and explains why the ticket values came out wrong.

rubric.criterion: Clarified the settlement rule and boundaries
rubric.strongAnswer: Asked about deductible exceeding approved, negative values, and the regression test before editing.
Reproduced and diagnosed the defect with no hints or one hint after a genuine attempt.
Reproduced, fixed, and added the batch method without destabilizing the base rule.
